verses.1: The LORD is king. Let the earth rejoice, let many isles be glad.
verses.2: Cloud and gloom surround him, righteousness and judgment are the foundation of his throne.
verses.3: Fire precedes him, and it burns around his enemies.
verses.4: His lightning lights up the world; the earth sees and trembles.
verses.5: The mountains melt like wax before the LORD, before the Lord of the whole earth.
verses.6: Declare the heavens his righteousness, and let all the peoples see his glory.
verses.7: Let all who make idols be put to shame, all who boast in false gods. Let every god bow to him.
verses.8: Zion heard and rejoiced, and the daughters of Judah were glad because of your judgments, O LORD.
verses.9: For you are the LORD most high over all the earth. You are exalted far above all gods.
verses.10: Let lovers of the LORD hate what is evil. The LORD protects the lives of his loyal ones; he rescues them from the hand of the wicked.
verses.11: Light is sown for the righteous, and for those upright in heart there is joy.
verses.12: Rejoice, you righteous, in the LORD, and give thanks to his holy name.

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: "it burns around his enemies" — the Hebrew phrase תְּלַהֵט סָבִיב ("it burns around") is interpreted as fire burning around his enemies.
- v. 7: "let every god bow to him" — the Hebrew uses "all gods" (כָּל־אֱלֹהִים), which is retained here as a literal reference to deities.
- v. 8: "daughters of Judah" — the plural "daughters" is retained as in the Hebrew (בְּנוֹת יְהוּדָה), though this may be metaphorical for the people.
